versions.changelog:
- A GPU whose OpenCL crashes while starting is reported as OpenCL not starting, instead of its tone mapping being not supported.
- Rockchip RK3588 results are no longer marked as unvalidated.

- Recognises hardware transcoding on Rockchip RK3588 instead of reporting it as software.
- A GPU with no VA-API driver, such as a Mali GPU, says so instead of suggesting a fix that can't help.
- Use this backend is shown as a button.

- Tests an AMD GPU whatever Hardware acceleration Jellyfin is set to.
- QSV on a GPU that isn't Intel says so, instead of suggesting a fix that can't help.
- A GPU that can only be tested while Jellyfin uses it now says which settings to change, on the Hardware Probe tab and Recommended Settings.

- The diagnostics zip can include the test results and measurements, with a checkbox on the Help tab that is off by default.
- Report on GitHub fills in the GPU, and ffmpeg shows whether it is jellyfin-ffmpeg instead of its path.
- The hardware report form requires the versions, ffmpeg, and backends, and takes the diagnostics zip as an upload.

- Every value in a suggestion table can be applied, except the server's own.
- No Internet streaming bitrate limit is recommended, since a limit transcodes videos that out of network devices could direct play.
- Recommendations and notes use Jellyfin's own wording, one point per line.
- Tone mapping suggestions show Jellyfin's help for each method, and applying VPP or VideoToolbox tone mapping also turns on Enable Tone mapping.
- The thread count and encoding preset suggestions recommend Auto, and the encoding preset names the slowest preset that keeps real time.
- The encoder presets suite tests every preset on the configured backend.
- Outputs that fall behind real time are listed one per row.
- The native and enhanced NVDEC decoder settings are recommended on.
- Performance Tests no longer measure trickplay.
- Performance test failures say what went wrong, and the same failure is listed once.
- Custom Test no longer selects audio codecs before an audio input is chosen.

- Performance Tests measure trickplay image generation on each backend and in software, with the Trickplay page's settings.
- Performance Tests measure audio transcoding of 21 audio formats in software, with a new Audio formats suite.
- Power is measured for AMD GPUs.

- Starting a probe or performance test shows its progress right away.
- A performance test set to cancel for transcodes no longer marks a later test as cancelled for one.
- Recommended Settings and Test Results load faster with many saved test results.
- An ffmpeg stuck in the graphics driver no longer blocks later probes until the server restarts.
- On Windows, a finished probe or an applied setting is no longer lost when the page reads the same file at that moment.
- Pages no longer show an error when saved results are deleted while they load.

- Suggestions show one table per setting.
- Auto is always the recommended encoding preset.

- Says when an output is too slow on every backend tested, with the fastest one.
- The Help tab lists test results and measurements with their size, each with its own delete.
- Deleting test clips keeps measurements.
- Test results take less disk space.

- Suggestions show as tables comparing each choice, with the recommended one marked and a reason.
- Related settings, such as deinterlacing and tone mapping, share one table.
- Adds a 4K test suite.
- Fixes Intel low-power, library video, and test suite comparisons.

- First stable release. Requires Jellyfin 12.2 or newer.
- Tests each hardware acceleration backend with short real transcodes, shows which ones work, and gives a fix for each one that doesn't.
- Says when Jellyfin can't open the GPU because of permissions, when a backend requires another platform or GPU vendor, and when Jellyfin, not the GPU, falls back to software.
- Tests QSV on every Intel adapter and AMF on the first AMD adapter on Windows, as Jellyfin picks them.
- Recommended Settings for each working backend and for software, including trickplay, deinterlacing, tone mapping, and Intel low power, with Apply, Revert, and a history.
- Warns when Jellyfin is set to a backend that doesn't work.
- Performance tests measure transcode speed and concurrent streams for each backend on test videos, film samples from 1080p to 8K, or a library file, with optional CPU, memory, GPU, and power use.
- Test suites compare encoder presets, qualities, tone mapping, deinterlacing, decoding, subtitle burn-in, audio, legacy formats, thread count, and Intel low power.
- Performance tests can reuse earlier measurements and pause while the server transcodes for a player.
- Test Results suggests a faster backend, flags outputs that fall behind real time, and suggests settings worth changing, with Apply and Revert.
- The Help tab has a diagnostics zip and a prefilled form for hardware reports, the cached test clips, Delete all data, and third-party notices.
- In the dashboard sidebar, fits phone screens, and works in any server language.
- A command-line version for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

name: HwProbe
description: Runs short test transcodes for each hardware acceleration backend and setting on the Transcoding and Trickplay pages. Shows which ones work, how to fix the ones that don't, and measures the performance of each. Recommended settings can be applied to Jellyfin's settings and reverted, or downloaded as a diagnostics zip to attach to an issue.
overview: Tests which hardware transcoding backends work on a Jellyfin server, and how fast each one transcodes
